title: Public evaluation of food safety: Changes and influencing factors from the perspective of social governance — Evidence from CSS data (2006–2023)
content:
by Han Lin

This study used descriptive analysis and multinomial logistic regression on seven‑wave Chinese Social Survey (CSS) data spanning 2006‑2023 to systematically examine long‑term trends and determinants of public food‑safety evaluation. Public food‑safety evaluation exhibited a phased “rise‑fall‑rise” mean score pattern across the study period. Level of social security showed a consistent significant positive correlation with food‑safety evaluation in all seven survey years (p < 0.001) with fluctuating‑yet‑growing effect sizes; for the “very safe vs. very unsafe” contrast, the odds ratio fell from 2.056 (2006) then rebounded to 2.201 (2023). In year‑stratified models, educational attainment had a stable negative association with food‑safety evaluation, whereas control‑variable effects including gender and age varied across survey waves. Statistically significant survey‑year‑by‑social‑security‑level interactions for most years indicated temporal fluctuation in the spill‑over effect of social governance on food‑safety evaluation. Model diagnostics revealed nearly all variance inflation factors (VIF) below 1.780, demonstrating no multicollinearity and robust conclusions. Comprehensive countermeasures — building a socially secure atmosphere, establishing food‑risk prevention and emergency‑response governance frameworks, and strengthening institutional trust to advance social‑governance performance — should be adopted to improve public food‑safety perceptions.
author: Han Lin
